whatFailed: A create call with a recipient that has no email correctly returns HTTP 400, but the JSON body is the tRPC/OpenAPI shape {message, code, data, issues} and carries neither the top-level `error` string nor the `statusCode` number that the getting-started guide publishes as the API's error response format.

docClaim.section: Error Handling / Error Response Format / Common Errors

observed: HTTP 400 with body {"message":"Input validation failed","code":"BAD_REQUEST","data":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","httpStatus":400,"path":"envelope.create"},"issues":[{"code":"invalid_union",...,"path":["payload","recipients",0,"email"],"message":"Invalid input"}]}. No `error` key, no `statusCode` key. Step 3 of the same scenario, which asserts only that a `message` exists (the shape common-workflows.md uses), passed against the identical request. Server stderr is empty; the product logged nothing abnormal.
impact: Integrators who follow the getting-started guide read `err.error` and `err.statusCode` off a failed call and get undefined for both, so their error handling surfaces nothing; no data loss, but the guide's error contract is fictional for every v2 endpoint.

rootCause.explanation: The v2 API is tRPC exposed through trpc-to-openapi 2.1.5 (packages/trpc/utils/openapi-fetch-handler.ts wraps createOpenApiNodeHttpHandler; packages/trpc/server/trpc.ts lines 39-67 is the only place Documenso customises the error body, and it only adds fields under `data`). trpc-to-openapi's node-http core builds every error body as {...errorShape, message, code, issues} typed as OpenApiErrorResponse {message, code, issues?}, and it rewrites the message to the literal 'Input validation failed' whenever the error is a BAD_REQUEST caused by a ZodError, putting the real detail in `issues`. Its OpenAPI generator emits the same three-field error schema, so Documenso's own published API reference (openapi.documenso.com, generated by packages/trpc/server/open-api.ts) documents {message, code, issues}. There is no code path anywhere in the v2 stack that can emit a top-level `error` or `statusCode` key; the HTTP status is only carried by the status line and, nested, as data.httpStatus. The guide's Error Response Format block and its three Common Errors examples were hand-written and have never matched the implementation. The docs even contradict each other: examples/common-workflows.mdx line 107 does `throw new Error(\`Failed to create envelope: ${error.message}\`)`, which is the real shape.

colleagueFinding.note: Their finding 5 ('every API error is labeled INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR at the top level, the real code one level down', scenario the-documented-error-envelope-on-an-unknown-envelope.api.1) is the same doc section seen from a different endpoint. This failure refines it in two ways. First, the top-level code is not always wrong: here it is BAD_REQUEST, because trpc-to-openapi maps a Zod input-validation failure straight onto the TRPCError code before any Documenso handler runs, whereas their case goes through an AppError re-thrown as a TRPCError and loses its code. Second, and independent of that, the envelope itself is wrong on every path: the documented `error` and `statusCode` keys do not exist in any v2 response, which is a docs defect rather than a product one, and their 'unreported' claim needs qualifying because community PR #3133 already documents the real shape for the rate-limit page.

notes: The scenario is not at fault: step 3 and step 4 send the identical request and were deliberately split because common-workflows.md and first-api-call.md publish contradictory failure shapes. Step 3 (message exists) passes, step 4 (error + statusCode) fails, which isolates the disagreement cleanly. Recommended fix for the doc author: replace the Error Response Format block in first-api-call.mdx with the real v2 body {"message": "Input validation failed", "code": "BAD_REQUEST", "data": {"code": "BAD_REQUEST", "httpStatus": 400, "path": "envelope.create"}, "issues": [...]}, say that the HTTP status is on the status line and mirrored at data.httpStatus, and rewrite the three Common Errors examples, since a missing recipient email never yields the human-readable 'Recipient email is required' string but a generic 'Input validation failed' with the field path under issues[].path. The v1 API under /api/v1 has its own, different error shape, so the page should say which version it is describing. Also worth flagging: the docs promise a self-describing message, and 'Input validation failed' plus a raw Zod invalid_union dump is a poor developer experience even once the docs are corrected.
